🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
Not yet confirmed as a defect — nothing in the shared save step is specific to this customer or to a case type, and the error record the system writes when a save genuinely fails has not been retrieved yet; that read will settle it. No previously-known recurring incident matches this symptom.

What we checked

  • The save step is common code used by every case type and every customer, with no customer-specific branch in it — consistent with the report that it hits many users across many case types, and against this being a setup problem on one case type.

  • When a save genuinely fails to write, the system undoes the whole thing and surfaces an error page carrying a unique reference code — so "a long wait, then back on the case screen with the data gone" is not what a failed write produces; if a reference code appeared on screen, it is the single most useful piece of evidence.

  • Our own performance records for this part of the product already show these case screens among the slowest in the application, and every case screen carries a fixed two-minute server-side limit on a single request.

Next

  • Get one concrete example from the customer: the case (or case type), the user, the exact date and time it happened, and a screenshot of whatever appeared on screen, including any reference code.

  • With that timestamp, pull the recorded errors and request timings for the incident application over that window, and check whether anything at all was written for that case.

Root cause: the Central Station Master screen on ADUSA's production Nettrack instance had a stale build (Last Build Date from 7/29), out of sync with the screen's current configuration, and the Azure App Service worker process was still serving the old compiled assembly in memory. This caused an HttpUnhandledException (HTTP 500) when loading the screen, which the customer experienced as the system "stalling" and losing entered data.

Escalation path that resolved it:

  1. Clear user cache → not sufficient

  2. Rebuild the screens (Screen Designer → "Build All Screens") → also not sufficient on its own

  3. Restart the Azure instance (web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack) → this resolved the wait, the slowness, and the error screen

Full documentation (analysis, ruled-out hypotheses, evidence, and screenshots for each step): https://trebuco.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AALPS/pages/478266851331/RCS-29234+LPMS+Case+Save+Failure+Technical+Documentation

Medical911

  1. We created two cases without making any changes, and both worked correctly.

  1. We added a data field, saved, and built the Medical911 page.

  1. We ran 3 tests and started seeing the errors Jim mentioned: the page reloads and loses the information entered, or loading becomes very slow.

  2. We removed the column and did Save and Build again. This time, saving took a very long time: we waited more than 30 minutes for the new incident's changes to save, and the tab never stopped loading.
